changes: General contract now permits arbitrary natural ambient dimension n, hypersurface degree d and pole parameter q over C[z_0,...,z_n]. Catalogue specializes n=5,d=6,q in {1,2}.

Explicitly requires F nonzero and homogeneous of degree d; source A has integer degree d(q+1)-(n+1); N_i has integer degree deg(D)+dq-n. Negative integer degree allows only zero. No separate homogeneity or nonvanishing condition is placed on Q.

HasCertificate now has explicit arguments F q A; n is inferred from AmbientPoly n and degree is F.totalDegree. Verify keeps explicit degree d in Verify F A d q D N Q; Verify.hasCertificate uses nonvanishing and homogeneity to identify d with totalDegree.
Optional witness JSON drops the independent d field; denominator degree is determined from D. The protected witness statement supplies HodgeSubmission.d (hypersurface degree).

The full cleared identity E=F^(q+1)Q, coprimality over C, arbitrary denominator degree, nonzero quotient permission and nonconstructive existence option remain. No new field-parity requirement is imposed.

changes: Current schemaVersion 2 acceptance.json is an attribution record: githubLogin, acceptedAt, and original pullRequest number/url. It carries no source hashes, verifier versions, workflow receipts or stored verification claims.
Publication reads the merged PR and records credit; current documentation expressly says it no longer inspects CI artifacts or requires particular merge parents. Retries retain attribution.

Accepted proof sources are now maintained in ordinary maintenance PRs, retaining original contributor, PR and date. Repository build rechecks changed proofs/witnesses/targets and affected applications. Editorial explanation changes require content checks but not Lean replay.

Shared library is built once, with separate affected-instance checks and shared-module kernel replay; toolchain, dependency and other non-Lean formal/lean changes select the full shared library and accepted applications.

Protected solve checks still compile in a sandbox, replay modules, audit the exact theorem/transitive axioms, pin checked base/head, and reject changed PR commits. A green solve/lean on maintenance means no new solve; it does not imply a fresh accepted solve.

Website publishes current main without authenticating historical proof sources or repeating premerge verification. Current source pins, historical acceptance and current CI/replay scope must be recorded separately.

book.publication_scope: Merged upstream mathematical exposition, as documented by Benjamin Diamond/benediamond commits and PR218, PR219, PR220. Record as author/maintainer-published claims; this monitor did not validate their proofs and does not treat them as protected Lean acceptance.
changes: New Chapter3B states divisor support for anti-invariant H3 of quasismooth sigma-invariant weighted sextic threefolds in P(1,1,1,1,2), via norm-contact curves, Abel-Jacobi derivatives, a finite spanning witness, openness and supported-projector specialization.

Its two-reflection theorem states all globally invariant H4 is divisor-supported for smooth globally Y-even sextics with an extra reflection in one X and one Y coordinate. Scope includes smooth 4+2 splits and independent transpositions in the two parity blocks; global evenness alone is insufficient.

New Chapter3C states all-target support for every smooth F(X,Y)=G(X,Q0(Y),Q1(Y),Q2(Y)), with three ternary quadrics and weighted-degree-six G, including singular/reducible discriminants and no additional linear symmetry. Point-pair incidence is the stated transfer mechanism. This is not an arbitrary six-mixed-quadrics theorem.

Chapter4 presents the complete 88-coefficient cyclic-six family for g=(X,zeta*y,zeta^-1*z0,zeta^-1*z1), g^3=tau, and asserts support through complementary deck/exchange quotients. This differs from the order-six action preserving cycle-q2.

Chapter2A retains the independent binary-sextic torsion-contact construction and raw/quintic Wronskian spanning statements. The book is reorganized as general mathematical treatments, not a list of checked example tuples.
The general globally Y-even sextic problem is still expressly open. Two-reflection and quadratic-net families have different/incomparable coefficient scope in the book.
book.literature_attribution: Chapter3B explicitly cites Voisin Proposition2.1 for the curve-correspondence strategy and Dolgachev for weighted residue/Lefschetz statements. The overview retains Diamond and Voisin references. No new rbajaj5 attribution was identified in the reviewed changes.
